description: Multiple Kani harnesses use String::from_utf8(...).expect(...) to construct test inputs from kani::any() bytes. Since kani::any() can produce invalid UTF-8, the harness itself can panic before reaching the function under test. This prevents Kani from proving panic-freedom of the target function even if inline asm support were added.
expected: Use kani::assume to restrict input domain to valid UTF-8 before unwrapping/expecting, rather than using expect which is a panic point
found: String::from_utf8(...).expect("valid UTF-8...") at input construction sites in 4 of 6 harness files
remediation: Replace expect with pattern: let s = match String::from_utf8(bytes) { Ok(s) => s, Err(_) => { kani::assume(false); unreachable!() } } to exclude invalid UTF-8 from verification domain without panicking
resolution_note: REPAIR-2: All .expect() calls replaced with kani::assume(false) pattern across all 6 harness files. 0 .expect() calls remain (confirmed by grep). 19 kani::assume(false) calls found across 5 harness files.
